Concepcion Pequena, Naga City 4400 Dear Atty. Tabora This has reference to your letter dated 28 November 2024 requesting for this Department's legal opinion and guidance regarding the following matters: I. Does the Local Government Units (LGUs) possess the legal authority to enact an ordinance granting a five-year franchise to operate a cockpit in the context of Presidential Decree No. 449 (Cockfighting Law of 1974), R.A. 7160 (Local Government Code), and any relevant DILG issuances? 2. What specific conditions and requirements must be met to maintain the validity of a five-year license to operate a cockpit? Per the representation, your client, Mr. Joel Vergara, is a substantial stakeholder in cockpit operations within the Municipality of Ragay. However, you alleged that the one- year validity of franchise hinders the return on investment required for the construction and ongoing maintenance of the cockpit arena. You then represented that Mr. Vergara intends to propose to the Sangguniang Bayan of Ragay to amend its ordinance by extending the franchise term of a cockpit for five years. Thus, the request for legal opinion. As to the first query, we answer in the affirmative. Please be informed that the LGUs has the authority to enact an ordinance granting a five-year franchise to operate a cockpit. While the LGC and PD 449 do not explicitly set a fixed validity period for a cockpit franchise, it provides LGUs discretion to determine how franchises are issued and for how long. Such laws, specifically Section 447 (a)(3)(v)1 of LGC, and Section 62 447. of PD 449, provide the LGUs the authority to grant franchises and regulate their terms through an ordinance. Thus, the Sangguniang Bayan has the power to authorize and grant franchise to the establishment, operation and maintenance of cockpits, and regulate cockfighting and commercial breeding of gamecocks within its territorial jurisdiction, provided that they adhere to PD 449 and other national regulations. As to the final query, to maintain a five-year franchise to operate a cockpit valid, the grantee must meet the specific conditions and standards outlined by the LGU in an ordinance granting the franchise, as well as conform with national laws and regulations. The operator must strictly adhere to the provisions of the local ordinance granting franchise and PD 449, including, but not limited to operating the cockpit only within the territorial jurisdiction of the LGU that granted the franchise, adhering to the prescribed days and times for cockfighting (e.g., Sundays, legal holidays, or during local fiestas), and ensuring the cockpit is located in an area designated for such operations under the LGU's zoning regulations. In addition, the franchise holder must pay the annual franchise fees, permits, and other required dues to the LGU within prescribed deadlines, and remit appropriate taxes related to cockpit operations, including amusement taxes and gambling-related taxes, to the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR). The franchise holder must likewise operate the cockpit in accordance with public interest and without causing interruptions or nuisances to the community. Further, please bear in mind that the LGUs may revoke or suspend the franchise if the grantee fails to comply with franchise conditions or LGU ordinances, engages in illegal activities (e.g., cockfighting on prohibited days or unauthorized betting), fails to pay required fees, taxes, or other dues, and violates safety, health, or animal welfare regulations. Violations or failure to comply with these requirements may result in penalties, suspension, or revocation of the franchise. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P.
